objects.description: Opaque handle to a proxy factory object from libproxy. The struct is forward-declared only; its contents are private and defined elsewhere. It represents a long-lived factory with internal caching used to resolve proxy configuration and compute proxy lists for URLs. Lifetime is managed manually; create with px_proxy_factory_new() and free with px_proxy_factory_free().

GType is a GLib fundamental type used for runtime type information in GObject. It is only referenced here via the function px_proxy_factory_get_type(); it is not defined in this header. Note: This entry is included only to acknowledge its presence; the actual type is defined by GLib, not this header.

functions.name: px_proxy_factory_new
functions.description: Creates a new pxProxyFactory instance used to resolve proxy settings for URLs. Intended to be kept for the lifetime of the application or as long as convenient to benefit from internal caching. Caller owns the returned object and should free it when done.
requirements: Caller assumes ownership of the returned pxProxyFactory and must release it with px_proxy_factory_free.
Do not use the pxProxyFactory after it has been freed.

functions.name: px_proxy_factory_get_type
functions.description: Returns the GType for pxProxyFactory (GLib type system). Pure function with no side effects (G_GNUC_CONST). Typically used for type registration/introspection in GLib/GObject contexts.

functions.name: px_proxy_factory_get_proxies
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated array of proxy configuration strings describing how to reach the given URL via proxies, in priority order. May block while reading configuration, evaluating PAC, or performing WPAD. Returns NULL on unrecoverable error. The caller must free the returned array using px_proxy_factory_free_proxies.
requirements: self must be a valid pxProxyFactory instance (created by px_proxy_factory_new) and not yet freed.
url must point to a valid, NUL-terminated URL string; behavior is unspecified if url is NULL or invalid.
The returned array is NULL-terminated and must be freed with px_proxy_factory_free_proxies when no longer needed.
The caller must handle a NULL return value as an unrecoverable error condition.
If multiple proxies are returned, the caller should attempt them in the given order (try the next if the first fails).
If a proxy string uses the socks scheme without version (socks://), the client MUST try SOCKS5 first and, on connection failure, fall back to SOCKS4.
If username:password are present in a proxy URL, the client should use them for authentication.

functions.name: px_proxy_factory_free_proxies
functions.description: Frees a NULL-terminated array of proxy strings previously returned by px_proxy_factory_get_proxies.
requirements: proxies must be a NULL-terminated array as returned by px_proxy_factory_get_proxies.
Call exactly once for a given proxies array; do not access the array or its strings after freeing.
Do not pass arrays not obtained from px_proxy_factory_get_proxies.

functions.name: px_proxy_factory_free
functions.description: Frees a pxProxyFactory instance and associated resources.
requirements: self must be a pxProxyFactory previously created by px_proxy_factory_new.
Call exactly once per instance; do not use self after it has been freed.
Ensure no concurrent use of self is in progress when freeing.

endpoints.name: px_proxy_factory_new
px_proxy_factory_get_type
px_proxy_factory_get_proxies
px_proxy_factory_free_proxies
px_proxy_factory_free

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated string representing a URL, typically in the form scheme://host[/path]. The scheme can be common values such as http, https, ftp, or socks variants (socks, socks5, socks4). The host should consist of alphanumeric characters, dots, and hyphens; an example default like example.com is valid. The optional path may contain slashes, alphanumerics, dashes, underscores, and dots. The overall length is typically bounded (e.g., up to around 1024 bytes).

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a URL string buffer to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR and related inputs
# for px_proxy_factory_get_proxies. The fuzzer stub constructs a URL from:
#   scheme:// + filtered(host_raw) + filtered(path_raw)
# We therefore generate two concatenated strings separated by a NUL so that a single
# buffer can be split by the fuzzer framework into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls if it
# uses slicing, or at least provide rich content for one call. The buffer will contain:
#   host_raw\0path_raw
# The stub applies filtering to host and path characters, so we prefer producing
# characters that survive filtering and also include some extras to explore edge cases.

SCHEMES = [
    "http", "https", "ftp", "socks", "socks5", "socks4"
]

HOST_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ".-"
PATH_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "/-_."
# Some additional characters that will be filtered out by the stub to test sanitization
EXTRA_NOISE = "!@#$%^&*()[]{}|`~:,?=+\t\n\r\x00\x01\x7f"

TLDS = [
    "com", "net", "org", "io", "dev", "local", "example", "co.uk", "de", "jp", "edu"
]

PATH_SEGMENTS = [
    "", "index.html", "login", "api", "status", "health", "v1", "v2", "download", "upload",
    "config", "pac", "wpad.dat", "data.json", "image.png", "sitemap.xml"
]


def _rand_label(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 63) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid leading/trailing hyphen per common DNS label rules; keep within stub filter
    if n == 1:
        return rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    middle_len = max(0, n - 2)
    middle = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-', k=middle_len))
    return rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) + middle + rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)


def _rand_host(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate diverse hostnames: simple, multi-label, IPv4-like (will be filtered ok), or mixed
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        # simple example.com style
        name = _rand_label(rng, 3, 12)
        tld = rng.choice(TLDS)
        return f"{name}.{tld}"
    elif choice < 0.50:
        # multi-label
        labels = [_rand_label(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 12)) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]
        return '.'.join(labels)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        # ipv4-like dotted quad
        parts = [str(rng.randint(1, 254)) for _ in range(4)]
        return '.'.join(parts)
    else:
        # include some noise that will be filtered out
        core = ''.join(rng.choices(HOST_CHARS, k=rng.randint(3, 20)))
        noise = ''.join(rng.choices(EXTRA_NOISE, k=rng.randint(0, 6)))
        return core + noise


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a path starting with '/' optionally, the stub will prepend if missing
    seg_count = rng.randint(0, 5)
    segments: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(seg_count):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            seg = rng.choice(PATH_SEGMENTS)
            if seg:
                segments.append(seg)
            else:
                segments.append('')
        else:
            length = rng.randint(1, 16)
            seg = ''.join(rng.choices(PATH_CHARS + EXTRA_NOISE, k=length))
            segments.append(seg)
    path = '/'.join(s for s in segments)
    # Occasionally ensure leading slash is absent to test stub insertion
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        path = '/' + path if not path.startswith('/') else path
    else:
        path = path.lstrip('/')
    # Limit length to what stub reserves
    return path[:127]


def _maybe_auth_in_host(rng: random.Random, host: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes prefix with user:pass@ to exercise auth parsing downstream in clients
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        user_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-"
        pass_chars = user_chars
        user = ''.join(rng.choices(user_chars, k=rng.randint(1, 8)))
        pwd = ''.join(rng.choices(pass_chars, k=rng.randint(0, 10)))
        if pwd:
            return f"{user}:{pwd}@{host}"
        else:
            return f"{user}@{host}"
    return host


def _build_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = rng.choice(SCHEMES)
    host = _rand_host(rng)
    host = _maybe_auth_in_host(rng, host)
    path = _rand_path(rng)
    url = f"{scheme}://{host}{path}"
    return url[:1024]


def _compose_buffer(url: str) -> bytes:
    # The stub creates url from two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls (host_raw, path_raw) and a chosen scheme.
    # To seed both, we provide two strings separated by NUL: host_raw\0path_raw.
    # We derive host_raw and path_raw from the URL for high validity.
    # Split scheme://host/path heuristically
    try:
        rest = url.split('://', 1)[1]
    except IndexError:
        rest = url
    # Extract host and path
    slash = rest.find('/')
    if slash == -1:
        host_raw = rest
        path_raw = ''
    else:
        host_raw = rest[:slash]
        path_raw = rest[slash:]
    # Ensure within bounds expected by stub reserve sizes
    host_raw = host_raw[:63]
    path_raw = path_raw[:127]
    payload = host_raw.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00" + path_raw.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
    # Keep total under 4096
    return payload[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    url = _build_url(rng)
    return _compose_buffer(url)
